4. Aesthetics
a. View
The only view of any consequence in the project is that of the Susquehanna River. The River can be seen from the area of Front Street and it can also be seen in part by looking down the various streets that intersect Front Street. Since the project does not include the installation of walls, dikes, or levees, the view will remain unobstructed, as now viewed from Front Street. Due to the closing of some streets and construction of buildings along Front Street the view from within the project may be restricted somewhat. Conversion of streets to walkways will not impact the view. In the case of the park or open spaces planned for the area, principally at the extreme south end of the project along Front Street, the view from the interior of the project along Second Street will be improved.
The possible impact on the view of the River from the construction of a levy, to protect the area from future floods, has been of major concern to the residents of the City. This will be discussed further in "Alternatives," Part IV.
The view of the project from the <u>West</u> bank of the River will be impacted by the new construction of high-rise apartments along Front Street. The nature of this impact is not known at this time, but it is not expected to be of an adverse nature.
b. Historic Preservation
As discussed previously in the description of the project, there are no structures as properties in the areas listed in the National Register of Historic Places. Therefore, project activities will not directly impact known properties of historical significance.
It is not known if any properties in the area will be nominated for the "Register" in years to come.
The extensive amount of scheduled property rehabilitation will preserve many of the older project properties that were built in the late 19th century. Therefore, a minor positive impact on the historic character of the area is anticipated.
